title: Make later-proof Intent comparison checks fast and stable under moderately high load

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-326#pass-later-proof-comparison-checks-under-load

Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: .planning/seeds/SEED-326-later-proof-comparison-checks-under-load.md#pass-later-proof-comparison-checks-under-load at implementation revision 3befd9f85715bca25a9fae107bf2bdb937455f36 (isolated detached scratch worktree /private/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-326-pass-later-proof-comparison-checks-under-load-scratch, clean before the probe).

Promise checked: "a provider-directed wait holds a later-provenance read, repeats ask nothing" (scope coverage bullet 5; key example "a repeat read during the wait asks again -> the provider-wait check fails"). Expected observable behavior: while the request owner's wait stands, a repeated later comparison read reaches GitHub with no request.

Choice among the suggestions: suggestion 2. Plan 589 slice 2 records that its only fault on this promise ("the request owner asks during a standing wait") failed the later provider-wait case at the first-read assertion, so the repeat-count assertion was never reached; this probe uses a different fault, specific to repeats, and does not repeat a recorded one. Suggestion 1 was examined by inspection and not probed: the collection path from a held pending observation to a kept build (landedCiCollectionLanding.ts, landedCiKeepResolution.ts, keptResolution, historyEntries) reads the slot's selection and the pending wait independently, so no single plausible fault was found that is specific to "later selection after a proof wait" without being the recorded selection/projection faults or a provenance-independent fault the equivalent real-server case exercises; a confirmed verdict there would need a contrived conjunction fault plus a 30-revision real-server witness. That remains unprobed, not disproved.

Fault (one, scratch only): src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/github-request-kept-admissions.mjs, KeptAdmissions.refusal(resource): after a held-back refusal is computed, the resource's admission is replaced with a fresh ReadAdmission, so a rate limit's wait ends with the first request it refuses instead of at its time ("nothing but its time ends it"). Fixtures and assertions were left intact.

Maintained check and assertion examined: dashboard/backend-tests/intent/intent-ci-comparison-pending-proof.spec.ts, case "later proof held by a provider-directed wait recovers after the controlled request-owner clock ends that wait", assertion `expect(clocked.server.github.calls.length).toBe(asked)` at line 142 (the repeat-count assertion).

Command (scratch root, each run): env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" npx playwright test --config dashboard/playwright.config.ts dashboard/backend-tests/intent/intent-ci-comparison-pending-proof.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list

Run observations (one-minute load 4.7-5.8):
- Baseline: 3 passed (13.1 s); later provider-wait case 2.5 s.
- Faulted: 1 passed, 2 failed (10.7 s). The later case passed its first-read assertions (`unavailable`, explanation) and its repeat `unavailable` assertion, then failed exactly at line 142: Expected 12, Received 20. This is the assertion that caught it; no earlier helper or assertion failed in that case. Also observed: the equivalent provider-wait sibling failed one line earlier, at line 141 (repeat read `none`, expected `unavailable`), so in the equivalent case the count assertion was again not reached; the equivalent malformed-listing case passed.
- Independent witness of reach and wrong behavior: a scratch spec (assertion-free copy of the later arrangement with the 429 held, printing fake-GitHub calls per read; untracked, deleted afterwards). Unfaulted: first read `unavailable` with 10 calls, repeat reads `unavailable` with 0 new calls each. Faulted: first read `unavailable` with 12 calls, each repeat read `unavailable` with 8 new calls (actions-workflow, four actions-runs, actions-run-artifacts for run 201, two actions-attempt-jobs). The promised behavior went wrong on the intended path — repeats asked GitHub during the standing wait — while the read's answer kind stayed `unavailable`, so only the count distinguishes it.
- Restoration: `git checkout` of the faulted file and removal of the witness spec; scratch `git status --short` empty and `git diff --stat` empty at HEAD 3befd9f85, matching the pre-probe state. Restored run: 3 passed (10.4 s).

Claim limit: the repeat-count assertion of the later provider-wait case catches a wait that lapses after its first refusal on this real-server path (dashboard read -> request owner -> synthetic gh -> fake GitHub). Nothing is claimed for other repeat faults or for the equivalent case's count assertion.

Next proof action: none required for this promise on the observed path; the later case's repeat-count assertion is now shown to catch a repeat-specific fault, which closes the note in plan 589 slice 2's fault table ("its repeat-count assertion is not reached"). If the caller wants the remaining suggestions evidenced, the missing observations are a fault against the same-owner-process assertion (suggestion 3) and a real-server witness of a later point after a proof wait (suggestion 1).

Prior disposition matched: plan 589 OB1 already disposes suggestion 1's gap as proved by composition; this probe adds no evidence for or against it and causes no new repair decision.

Cleanup: scratch edits restored and verified as above; the scratch worktree was removed (`git worktree remove`, `git worktree prune`; path absent, no SEED-326 entry in `git worktree list`). No commit, push, stash, reset, clean or branch switch was made in the project checkout, and no file there was edited by this check. Observed, not mine: the project checkout now shows an uncommitted change to dashboard/tests/intent-ci-comparison-proof.md (3 insertions, 3 deletions, file time 14:52 local, during this check's read-only lookup phase); it was left untouched.

Cost:
- Test runtime: 51.3 s measured, the sum of Playwright's reported totals for five runs (baseline 13.1 s, baseline witness 5.7 s, faulted 10.7 s, faulted witness 5.7 s, restored 10.4 s); excludes scratch dependency setup, which was not timed separately.
- Human effort: unavailable — no human took part and no measure was recorded.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a measured figure — no token or step meter was exposed to this agent; estimated 15 tool invocations, counted from this run.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 228387 ms (measured), from 1794466335022 to 1794466563409 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

---

Wrap-up disposition

- Checked revision: 3befd9f85715bca25a9fae107bf2bdb937455f36.
- Evidence: the report above; one probe, verdict Caught. It does not protect the whole story.
- Decision: no follow-up. The report names no actionable gap. The two unprobed suggestions stay as recorded: the same-owner-process assertion has no fault control, and a later point after a proof wait is owned by composition (the in-process judgment check plus the public later point in landed-ci-history-pending-sources.spec.ts), because the story keeps real-server history inside the revision walk.
- Follow-up links: none.
